items.article: Gary Sutton's scheduled execution has been paused after Tennessee Governor Bill Lee halted remaining 2026 executions following Christa Pike's failed lethal injection. Gary Wayne Sutton, a Tennessee death row inmate, has had his execution paused after Governor Bill Lee suspended all remaining executions in the state for 2026 following the failed execution of Christa Pike . Sutton was convicted of the 1992 killings of siblings Tommy Griffin and Connie Branam and has spent three decades on death row. Sutton was scheduled to receive a lethal injection on December 3, but Lee’s order to suspend executions for the rest of the year means the sentence will not be carried out as planned. Sutton, 61, was convicted in 1992 alongside his uncle, James Dellinger, for the murders of Tommy Griffin and Griffin’s sister, Connie Branam. The pair were sentenced to life in prison, and later received death sentences for Griffin’s murder. Dellinger died in prison in 2023 aged 71. Griffin, 24, was found shot in the back of the head near the Little River on February 24, 1992. Branam, 34, was discovered five days later inside her burned vehicle. At the time, Griffin’s family reported an ongoing feud between their family and Sutton’s before the killings.

items.article: Many consumers are likely on the hook for an increase of about 10% or more in 2027, experts said. Many consumers face much higher health insurance premiums and cost-sharing next year, as factors like increased use of GLP-1 drugs , the expiration of enhanced Obamacare subsidies and a high U.S. inflation rate push up costs across the healthcare system, experts said. The dynamic is stressing household budgets at a time when they're already strained by broader affordability issues , a key issue in the upcoming midterm elections. "They can expect to pay more," said Jonathan Oberlander, a professor of health policy and political science at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. "Not just in terms of premiums — but also in terms of deductibles and copayments." Most Americans under age 65 — about 166 million people — get health insurance via employer-sponsored health plans. Employers generally subsidize the cost of health insurance for their workers by covering a large portion of their monthly premium payments. The average worker paid $6,850 of annual premiums in 2025, while employers contributed more than $20,000 per worker, according to KFF, a health policy research group. In 2027, the cost for employers to provide health benefits will rise by an estimated 8.2% per worker, on average — the largest increase since 2003, even after accounting for cost-reduction measures by employers, according to Marsh, a consulting firm.

Tadaryl Shipp joined his then-girlfriend, Christa Pike, in killing their Job Corps classmate, Colleen Slemmer Christa Pike was not alone when she bludgeoned her classmate Colleen Slemmer to death – so why was she the only perpetrator who received the death penalty? According to court documents, Pike, her then-boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and their friend Shadolla Peterson lured Colleen into the woods near their dormitory in Knoxville, Tennessee , in January 1995. Pike and Shipp spent the following 30 minutes brutally attacking the 19-year-old with various weapons while Peterson stood guard. Pike, then 18, would be the one responsible for ending Colleen's life, hitting her on the back of her head with an asphalt rock. It's believed that Pike was the one who came up with the plan, believing Colleen to have been romantically interested in Shipp at the time. But scholars be damned, I’m having a lot of fun playing The Witcher 3 in 2026, and I’m not ashamed of it. The pleasure of rediscovering this classic also made me appreciate even more the excellent job that developer CD Projekt Red did in adapting Andrzej Sapkowski’s fantasy world in a way that is respectful and faithful, even if not entirely accurate to the source material. CD Projekt Red released The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered on Sept. 29, a free (on most platforms) update to the classic 2015 RPG that brings massive improvements to the game’s graphics, plus some much-needed fixes to gameplay elements. It’s no surprise, then, that Geralt’s most famous adventure is suddenly the highest-rated game of 2026 (well, on a technicality). items.article: Leigh was strength training four times a week, walking 10K steps a day, yet the scales kept climbing. After doctors repeatedly told her to exercise more, a shocking photo forced her to search for answers. For a long time, Leigh Woods avoided paying too much attention to her reflection. At 110kg, she didn't particularly like looking at herself in the mirror and had become good at avoiding it. Then she spotted a side-on photograph of herself in a workplace newsletter. 'I was just like, "Oh, is that what I look like? I need to do something about it,"' the 35-year-old, from Sydney , tells the Daily Mail. By then, Leigh's confidence had taken a hit. She was going out less and didn't particularly want to be seen. Even her motivation was beginning to suffer, although she was still getting herself to the gym. That was the part she couldn't understand. Leigh wasn't someone who had stopped exercising as her weight climbed. She was strength training four mornings a week, aiming for 10,000 steps a day and fitting in cardio sessions, while also paying attention to her nutrition. Yet she estimates she was gaining around 10kg a year. After years of trying to shift it, Leigh had started wondering whether the problem was her. 'Am I actually doing what I'm meant to be doing?' she remembers thinking. 'Am I just lying to myself? Should I just add in more exercise?'

items.text: What's really going on with the lymphatic drainage beauty trend videos?
items.article: Fans of these massages claim they "depuff" and "define" their stomach - but what's actually happening to their bodies? If she's ever feeling bloated, Abbey Alexandra has a go-to routine, using body oil and a wooden roller to perform stomach massages. The 31-year-old from Birmingham shares before-and-after videos on TikTok, saying she feels the process leaves her depuffed and defined: "You definitely feel a lot better after, they are relaxing." The technique is a form of lymphatic drainage massage, adapted from a medical treatment and shared as a beauty trend. Celebrity fans include Maya Jama, who shares her clinic sessions, and actress Hailey Bieber, who told Time magazine: "I swear by them." Whether there is a physical change - or any need for one - is debatable, but fans of the massages claim they help "flatten" and "debloat" and give a "snatched waist" and "sculpted abs". But what's actually happening to their bodies? Many videos on social media promoting lymphatic massage show a woman either standing sideways, facing the front or perhaps lying down with her stomach showing a slight - and very normal - curve outwards. Then begins the methodical massage in circular motions seemingly draining fluid away. By the end, her stomach appears flatter - if a little red.

items.article: Lola Young recently said it left her lungs feeling “battery-powered”. Recently, singer Lola Young claimed that vaping had affected her voice and made it harder for her to breathe. In a TikTok, the 25-year-old shared: “Somebody once said to me, ‘Lola, there will be a day when you wake up, you’ll be 25 or 26, from a deep sleep, and you’ll start to feel the effects of vaping’... The day has come. “My lungs feel like they’re battery-powered, like they’re just one big battery. “Breathing feels like a chore; it feels like hard work, it feels like I should be paid for breathing. It feels like there will be no tomorrow”. Speaking to HuffPost UK, Girish Desai , Chief Pharmacist at Landys Chemist , said that while “Vaping is less harmful than smoking and can be a useful way for smokers to quit cigarettes... we should not confuse less harmful with harmless”. Though the NHS’s site agrees that it’s a better alternative than smoking, they also say it’s “not harmless” and that we still don’t know what its long-term effects might be. They added that kids and non-smokers should “never” vape. Meanwhile, a Nature article suggests that those who begin vaping as children might see “bigger health risks than we’d thought”, with potential lung issues “just the tip of the iceberg”.
